newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to bar entry of suspect visitors during APEC.
newsitem.headline: Manila to bar entry of suspect visitors during APEC.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos ordered immigration officials on Saturday to bar entry to the Philippines of anyone who might disrupt the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit he will host next month.
"As host of this year's APEC meetings, we must be diligent in enforcing all security measures, which in our best judgement are necessary to prevent disturbances," Ramos in a statement.
Government officials declined to say if this meant a ban on the entry of of East Timorese resistance leader and Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta.

Ramos-Horta, who won this year's Nobel peace prize with East Timor's Roman Catholic bishop Carlos Belo, has accepted an invitation to speak at an international meeting of non-government organisations (NGOs) in Manila on November 21-24.
The meeting is being held in parallel with the November 22-23 meeting of APEC foreign ministers and the summit on November 25.
Ramos said he had ordered the Department of Foreign Affairs not to issue visas to any foreigners who could pose a threat.
Philippine immigration officials last week denied entry to about 100 East Timorese on suspicion that they planned protests in Manila next month to press Indonesia to leave East Timor.
Indonesian President Suharto is expected to attend the leaders' summit of the 18-member APEC forum.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move never recognised by the United Nations.
The Ramos government barred Ramos-Horta and other East Timorese dissidents from entering the country in 1994 during an international human rights conference on East Timor.
